title: Model intake-to-launch sprint playbook for catalog additions
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: Provide a repeatable, sprint-friendly playbook for taking a new model from intake through catalog listing, benchmarks, docs, and coordinated external announcements. This ticket codifies responsibilities, gating criteria, artifacts to produce, communication cadence, and post-launch validation so cross-functional teams (Product, Eng, Design, Docs, Growth, Support, SRE, Legal) can execute with minimal back-and-forth and predictable timelines. Scope: new model additions to the public model catalog (hosted + dedicated compatibility), including benchmark signals, SDK updates, console metadata, release notes, and launch communications. Out of scope: model training, research-level evaluations, or ad-hoc enterprise-only private deployments (handled by separate Private onboarding playbook).
checklist: Intake: capture model metadata (architecture, checkpoint, intended tasks, license, owner) in intake form and attach to ticket
Security & legal check: confirm license & IP restrictions and record legal sign-off (if required)
Compatibility triage: ENG to validate model works in serving runtime and note memory/cost profile (ENG-4210)
Benchmark plan: define dataset slices, latency/cost SLOs, and quality metrics; assign benchmark owner
Run bench: reproduce baseline runs and post results to benchmark dashboard; tag regressions >5%
Console & catalog metadata: Design + PM to prepare short description, model card, example prompts, and recommended usage guidance
SDK + API: engineering to add model key to model catalog API, update SDK enum, and add generation/embedding samples
Docs: write or update docs page with quickstart, promps, sample responses, and migration notes
Release notes: PM to draft human-friendly release notes and a technical appendix (format for changelog)
PRs & review: open PRs for runtime changes, SDK, docs; collect engineering & design review approvals
End-to-end test: QA to run smoke tests against hosted and dedicated variants, confirm fallback behavior
Observability: SRE to add cost/latency dashboards, set up error rate alerts and throttling rules
Canary rollout: coordinate a canary rollout window (24–72h) and failure rollback criteria
Marketing & comms: finalize blog/social copy, support KB article, and customer-facing examples
Launch day checklist: schedule announcement, monitor dashboards, standup rotations, and update status page
Post-launch 7/30 day review: collect metrics (usage, latency, quality regressions, support tickets) and run retrospective
release_notes_draft: Headline: Add <ModelName> to Redwood model catalog — faster, cheaper generation for NLU tasks. Technical appendix: model size, tokenization differences, known regressions, shortcuts for parameter tuning, recommended quantization and batching profiles. Migration notes: behavior differences vs existing models and example prompts. SDK usage snippets included.
communication_plan: Week -2: Intake confirmation to stakeholders. Week -1: Preview benchmark highlights to Docs/Support/Growth. 3 days before: Draft release notes and announcement for review. 24h before: Final sign-off from Eng/SRE/Legal. Launch day: Coordinated posts (blog + changelog) + social snippets + support readiness email. Post-launch week: daily monitoring sync for first 72h, then twice-weekly for first 14 days. Channels: #pm-catalog, #eng-runtime, #benchmarks, #growth, weekly launch review meeting.
gating_criteria: Benchmarks: Quality delta within agreed threshold vs baseline or documented trade-offs accepted
Runtime: Passing smoke tests and canary with latency within SLOs
Docs: Public-facing docs and SDK samples published
Legal: License clearance obtained if required
Support: KB article and triage runbook available
post_launch_tasks: 72h: Compile incidents and anomalies; run immediate rollback if critical errors observed
7d: Usage and quality report published to stakeholders
30d: Performance review and decision: promote wider availability, tune defaults, or deprecate
Ongoing: Add model to Optimize recommendations if cost/quality merits inclusion
benchmarks_requirements: Datasets: include representative slices for NLU/QA/safety where applicable
Metrics: latency p50/p95, tokens/sec, cost-per-token, generation-quality F1/ROUGE/other task-specific metrics
Reproducibility: attach seed and config; CI job to reproduce smoke bench
Failure thresholds: set clear cutoffs for unacceptable regressions
observability_requirements: Per-model latency p50/p95 by region and instance class
Error rate and stack traces sampling for first-responder debugging
Alerting: paging thresholds for total errors and cost spikes
risk_mitigation: Fallback models: pre-configure compatible lower-cost model variant for automatic fallback
Rate limits: set conservative default quotas during canary
Rollback plan: one-click config to disable model routing and revert traffic
Customer communication: pre-drafted statements for known behavior changes
